newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta stocks close slightly up on secondaries.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta stocks close slightly up on secondaries.

text.p: Jakarta stocks edged up at the close on Friday, despite continued selling on some blue chip stocks, after active buying in secondaries, brokers said.
"Foreign investors continuously sold some blue chip issues and it put pressure on the overall market sentiment," an analyst with a Japanese firm said.
She believed growing concern on domestic political tensions ahead May 29 general election would put further pressure on the market in the coming week.
The Jakarta Composite Index rose 0.09 points, or 0.01 percent, to close at 657.07 points after earlier falling to 654.68 points.
Compared to last Friday's closing of 673.69 points, the Jakarta index has fallen about 2.47 percent on the week.
Gainers led losers by 55 to 42, with 82 counters unchanged.
Total turn-over was estimated at about 447.8 billion rupiah compared to 474 billion rupiah on Thursday.
Chemical firm Eterindo Wahana was the most active stock during the day, boosting sentiment on other stocks in the chemical sector such as Sorini and Aneka Kimia Raya, brokers said.
Eterindo made sharp gains after its debut on Friday, closing at a price of 1,575 rupiah, compared with its offer price of 1,300 rupiah. About 49.7 million shares in the stock changed hands.
Secondary shoe maker Kasogi International also made sharp gains on active buying on its plan to propose rights issue soon, brokers said.

A company official said the firm planned to propose a one-for-one rights issue at a price of 1,000 rupiah to raise about 63 billion rupiah. It closed 100 rupiah higher at a price of 1,275 rupiah on a volume of 9.1 million shares.
Retailers Multipolar and Matahari Putra Prima were also active on the expectation of good first quarter results, brokers said.
Blue chip counters such as Semen Gresik, Sampoerna and Gudang Garam, Indosat and Citra Marga were among the losers, brokers said.
Cement maker Semen Gresik closed 5.11 percent lower at 5,575 rupiah on active selling with about 2.3 million shares changing hands, they said.
"I believe the selling of Semen Gresik also was triggered by the perception that its first quarter result was not in line with market expectations," a broker with European securities firm said.
Company officials were not immediately available for comment.
